claim: Stock backward scatters dQ with atomics; splitting removes them
finding: Stock assigns disjoint dQ and dK/dV programs within one launch; dQ uses tl.store. Captured-buffer gradients are a separate atomic path. Stock already has two tile pairs. Separate launches permit independent compiler settings.

claim: Backward is five matmuls per tile and about 2.5x forward FLOPs
verdict: not an accurate count of these implementations
finding: The ideal algebra has five matmuls when reconstructed intermediates can be shared. This template separately recomputes QK and dP in dQ and dK/dV traversals. Avoid a numerical FLOP ratio in this section.

claim: Early dP overlaps matrix work with exponentials and cuts an illustrative 17 units to 12
verdict: dependency change supported; hardware overlap and numerical timing unverified
finding: dP=dO V^T does not depend on reconstructed P. Selected paths move it earlier. A dependency graph is appropriate; a measured timeline requires profiling.

claim: Panel dots and dV fragments reduce registers and avoid spills
verdict: source transformation supported; resource improvement requires native-code comparison
finding: D96/D192/D256 products are split into panels. Some dV paths use 64-column fragments; the FP16 query-first path uses 32-column fragments. Do not generalize all paths as two 64-column views.

claim: XCD remapping pins each head to an XCD and improves L2 hits
finding: The code permutes logical program IDs using an eight-XCD model. It neither binds programs to physical XCDs nor proves improved cache hit rate. State intent to improve locality. MI350 has eight XCDs and 4 MB L2 per XCD in the AMD architecture documentation.

claim: Reversing causal dQ rows launches the longest work first and shortens the tail
verdict: mapping supported; dispatch order and performance effect need evidence
finding: Reversal puts the largest causal rows at the earliest logical program IDs. Actual hardware scheduling and tail reduction are not established by this code alone.

claim: Query-first traversal shares kv_num_blocks and kv_indices across query heads
verdict: mechanism valid but metadata names wrong
finding: The dK/dV query-first traversal shares the Q block metadata traversal (Q_NUM_BLKS / Q_IDX), while each query head retains its own tensor accesses.

claim: All users automatically receive the reported speedups
finding: Automatic selection is guarded by exact gfx950 shapes, layouts, mask, scale, score modification and options. The PR body reports explicit-option results on an installed build with source overlays and explicitly leaves automatic indexed-path performance pending. Independently benchmark actual automatic selection.

claim: Merged backward tuning was measured on dense attention
finding: The original local scripts call q>=kv causal attention dense. GQA cases are causal; block-sparse cases use a causal window of 1024. New results record masks explicitly.
